The diff-relative conformance test compares each port against its named baseline: the port may not introduce a network/DB/execution construct the baseline did not already contain. An unlisted file fails the test, so a new file cannot enter the capability surface without a declared origin.
_ruling: 2026-08-01 founder: port faithfully including existing behaviour. The claim under review is 'introduces no network surface the source did not have' — NOT absolute read-only proof. See adversarial-review spec-writing standard.

_baseline_verified_by_hand._note: Capabilities whose baseline safety properties are load-bearing require a hand-established baseline BEFORE porting, recorded here. Capability 6 (operator-gateway) is the one that needs it — its whole safety story is 'no live runner, no real execute button'. 'No new surface' is worthless against an unexamined baseline.

_imports_note: Import-level provenance. judgment must be one of: same | different-but-checked | must-change. UNDECLARED fails the suite exactly as an undeclared FILE does. File provenance proves origin; this proves the imports still mean what they meant.

REBUILT, now against createUniteGroupServerClient (was this app's Pi-CEO-scoped createServerClient until the wrong-Supabase-project bug was fixed — see the imports map entry for this file below). The source imports getUser+createClient from its own @/lib/supabase/server (anon-key, RLS-enforced, per-user). The same specifier originally resolved here to a service-role client with no per-user identity; it still does, just scoped to the correct project now. A verbatim port would have typechecked while silently swapping an RLS-enforced read for an RLS-bypassing one. No source baseline applies, so it is excluded from diff-relative comparison by design.

_target_native.lib/supabase/unite-group-server.ts: NEW file of THIS app, added to fix a real production bug: wiki_pages lives in the Unite-Group prod Supabase project (lksfwktwtmyznckodsau), not Pi CEO's own project (zbryrmxmgfmslqzizsto) that lib/supabase/server.ts reaches. The wiki-graph route and page were both calling the wrong client (lib/supabase/server.ts — no longer in this capability's import graph now that both call sites were repointed), so every read hit the wrong project's PostgREST endpoint, got a 404, and surfaced as an opaque 500. This file gives wiki-graph its own client scoped to the correct project. No source baseline applies; diff-relative comparison is meaningless for it.

auth gate.reason: EXPECTED, and now PROVEN rather than asserted. The source's getUser()/redirect('/auth/login') gate is removed: per-user auth has no equivalent here (single operator, no identity). The gate moved layer - it is now proxy.ts. The FIRST version of this reason said 'auth is enforced upstream by proxy.ts, whose matcher covers all non-static routes and 401s without a session', and that was FALSE. The matcher does cover every non-static route, but proxy() only checks a session for paths listed in PROTECTED_PAGE_PREFIXES / PROTECTED_API_PREFIXES, and /command-centre was in neither - so all four command-centre pages and the wiki-graph API served anonymous requests while reading wiki_pages through a service-role client that bypasses RLS. __tests__/command-centre-auth-coverage.test.ts calls proxy() directly with no cookie and proved it: 5 failed against 2 passing positive controls, so the red was not vacuous. /command-centre and /api/command-centre were then added to the protected prefixes and it went 7/7. This exemption's reason is now the tested behaviour of a named file rather than a sentence.

database client.reason: History: `await createClient()` (anon-key, RLS-enforced) was first replaced by `createServerClient()` (this app's Pi-CEO-scoped client), which read 1 -> 2 under the tracked regex (import specifier + call site of the same renamed function, not two clients). That client turned out to reach the wrong Supabase project - wiki_pages lives in Unite-Group prod, not Pi CEO's project - so it was replaced again with `createUniteGroupServerClient()`. That name does not contain the literal substrings `createServerClient` or `createClient(`, so the tracked regex now counts 0 in this file: not because the client disappeared, but because the count is textual, not semantic, and a renamed call site stops matching. A decrease is not flagged by the TRACKED test (it only fails on an increase), so this entry exists for documentation honesty, not to pass a check. What it does NOT excuse, either time: the privilege level. Both clients are service-role and bypass RLS - only which project is reached has changed.

_declared_deltas_note: Per-file, per-rule expected divergences, each naming the EXACT count transition it excuses (from -> to) plus a reason. Only that one measured transition is exempt: any other magnitude, in the same file under the same rule, still fails. Keying on file+rule alone - the first design - was a blanket exclusion wearing a narrower label, and cross-vendor review caught it: declaring 'auth gate' on a file excused every future auth-gate loss in that file, forever. Second lesson from the same review: a reason must be checkable against something. 'Enforced upstream by proxy.ts' read as evidence, was not, and was wrong - until a test made it both.
_privilege_note: privilege is required on an import ENTRY exactly when that import resolves to an in-repo module which constructs a privileged database client (a client built from a *SERVICE_ROLE* or *SERVICE_KEY* env var, which bypasses Row Level Security). The check derives the privileged set by reading the resolved modules, so a module that BECOMES privileged without any import changing is still caught — the case none of the existing map checks can see, because they only compare the map against the set of import specifiers. Declaring privilege on an import that does NOT resolve to such a module is also a failure: a stale claim inflates the map the same way a phantom entry does.
